Inclined to find fault or criticize.

examples.text: A good teacher is fair but critical.

glosses: Pertaining to, or indicating, a crisis or turning point.

examples.text: This is a critical moment.

Such a scandal as the prosecution of a brother for forgery—with a verdict of guilty—is a most truly horrible, deplorable, fatal thing. It takes the respectability out of a family perhaps at a critical moment, when the family is just assuming the robes of respectability: […] it is a black spot which all the soaps ever advertised could never wash off.

glosses: Extremely important.

examples.text: It's critical that you deliver this on time.

Oxygen levels on Earth skyrocketed 2.4 billion years ago, when cyanobacteria evolved photosynthesis:[…]. The evolutionary precursor of photosynthesis is still under debate, and a new study sheds light. The critical component of the photosynthetic system is the “water-oxidizing complex”, made up of manganese atoms and a calcium atom.
Third Pole glaciers are critical to billions of people from Vietnam to Afghanistan.

glosses: Relating to criticism or careful analysis, such as literary or film criticism.

examples.text: The movie was a critical success, but bombed at the box-office.

“Unless you are purchasing cereal from a health food store, many brands that are marketed as healthy are usually full of sugar and processed ingredients,” says Garcia.
 So when you’re choosing cereal, bread or any other whole-grain product, Garcia recommends reading labels with a critical eye.

Essential or decisive for determining the outcome or future of something; extremely important; vital.

examples.text: A secure supply of crude oil is crucial for any modern nation, let alone a superpower.
The battle of Tali-Ihantala in 1944 is one of the crucial moments in the history of Finland.

The perfume industry is facing a major problem: maintaining constant levels of quality is crucial, but it is increasingly difficult to obtain a regular supply of all the necessary natural ingredients.

Vocabulary provides a foundation from which grammar, phonology, and morphology emerge, and in a subject area it provides access to conceptual knowledge. Vocabulary selection for pedagogical purposes is therefore crucial.
Language is crucial because it is the best weapon against violence. When children don’t have the words to express their thoughts, they raise their fists.

glosses: Cruciform or cruciate; cross-shaped.
